Package hadur2.core.physics

Class Rules

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.physics.Rules
public final class Rules extends Object
The Robocode game rules the core relies on, identical to robocode.Rules.

The core may not import the engine (CORE-1), so the constants and formulas it needs are copied here; PhysicsMatchesEngineProperties and EnergyLedgerProperties check every one against the engine's own. Units are the engine's: distances in pixels, time in ticks (turns), velocities in px/tick, energy in energy points and, unlike the rest of the core, the turn rates in degrees per tick (use getTurnRateRadians(double) for radians).

The energy formulas are what the EnergyLedger uses to explain an enemy's energy changes, so only a drop spent on a bullet becomes a wave (WAVE-1); MIN_BULLET_POWER and MAX_BULLET_POWER are the [0.1, 3.0] range a corrected drop must fall in (WAVE-2).

  • Method Details

    • getTurnRate

      public static double getTurnRate(double velocity)
      Degrees per tick a robot can turn at velocity: 10 standing, falling by 0.75 per px/tick of speed to 4 at full speed. A fast robot turns wide.
      Parameters:
      velocity - the robot's velocity, in px/tick (either sign)
      Returns:
      the body's turn limit, in degrees per tick

    • getTurnRateRadians

      public static double getTurnRateRadians(double velocity)
      getTurnRate(double) in radians per tick, the unit the movement predictor works in.
      Parameters:
      velocity - the robot's velocity, in px/tick (either sign)
      Returns:
      the body's turn limit, in radians per tick

    • getBulletSpeed

      public static double getBulletSpeed(double power)
      A bullet's speed: 20 - 3 × power, so from 11 px/tick at power 3.0 to 19.7 at 0.1. As in the engine, the power is first clamped to [MIN_BULLET_POWER, MAX_BULLET_POWER].
      Parameters:
      power - the bullet's power, in energy
      Returns:
      the bullet's speed, in px/tick

    • getBulletDamage

      public static double getBulletDamage(double power)
      Energy a bullet of power takes from the robot it hits: 4 × power, plus 2 × (power - 1) above power 1, so 16 at power 3.0. Unlike getBulletSpeed(double), the power is not clamped (the engine's is not either).
      Parameters:
      power - the bullet's power, in energy
      Returns:
      the damage, in energy

    • getBulletHitBonus

      public static double getBulletHitBonus(double power)
      Energy the shooter gets back when its bullet hits: 3 × power. This refund can hide a shot fired on the same tick from a raw energy reading, which is why the ledger adds it back (WAVE-1).
      Parameters:
      power - the bullet's power, in energy
      Returns:
      the refund, in energy

    • getWallHitDamage

      public static double getWallHitDamage(double velocity)
      Energy a robot loses hitting a wall at velocity: |velocity| / 2 - 1, and none at 2 px/tick or slower. At full speed it is 3.0, the same as the strongest bullet, so a wall hit on its own can pass for a shot unless the ledger explains it (WAVE-1).
      Parameters:
      velocity - the speed at impact, in px/tick (either sign)
      Returns:
      the damage, in energy, never negative

    • getGunHeat

      public static double getGunHeat(double power)
      Gun heat a shot of power adds: 1 + power / 5. A gun can fire only at heat 0, and cools by the battle's cooling rate (0.1 by default) each tick, so a power-3.0 shot holds the gun 16 ticks at the default rate.
      Parameters:
      power - the bullet's power, in energy
      Returns:
      the heat the shot adds
